subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, and operators?
rationale: The code can plausibly build on existing Gateway event primitives, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes product scope, security expectations, and public CLI/config surface.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent or explicitly scoped session set, and defer bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces, but require explicit delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy before implementation.

options.title: No core mode
options.body: Keep raw logs, existing session selection, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid a core cross-channel TUI mirror feature.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `openclaw tui --observe` style mode that only shows authorized activity for a selected agent or explicitly scoped session set, and defer bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The current TUI isolation behavior and dominant TUI/Gateway session history route through steipete, making this the best available owner for the product boundary decision.
